newsitem.title: JORDAN: Israel's new ambassador arrives in Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Israel's new ambassador arrives in Jordan.

text.p: Israel's new ambassador to Jordan Oded Eran arrived in Amman on Monday and presented his credentials to Jordanian Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawneh.

Eran, formerly Deputy Director General for Economic Affairs at the Foreign Ministry, is Israel's second ambassador to Jordan since the two countries opened up embassies two years ago following their 1994 peace treaty.

Since the peace accord was signed Jordan has been seen as the Arab state closest to Israel. But the treaty was opposed by some Jordanians and dissatisfaction grew when a much-promised economic dividend failed to materialise.
In March a Jordanian soldier shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls near the border between the two countries. The shooting was followed by a number of other attacks on Israelis and Israeli interests.
Israel said on Monday Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan would meet on Tuesday for talks at the site of the March shootings.

Tarawneh, appointed in March when King Hussein picked Abdul-Salam al-Majali to form a new government, said on Sunday his ministry would work hard to promote Jordanian business both with Arab countries and with Israel.
"He's a friend of mine. He's an economist, I'm an economist. We're going to discuss economics," he said of Monday's meeting with Eran.
